extra.message: The notification_mark_read endpoint uses an insecure direct object reference (IDOR). The notification_id is taken directly from the URL path (line 164: get_object_or_404(Notification, pk=notification_id, recipient=request.user)). Although Django returns a 404 when the notification doesn't belong to the user, an attacker can enumerate notification IDs to confirm existence and timing-based side channels reveal whether a notification exists, enabling reconnaissance of other users' activities.

Multiple JSON API endpoints are decorated with @csrf_exempt, disabling CSRF protection for authenticated API operations. Affected endpoints: whoami (line 61-64), employees_list (line 76-81), employee_detail (line 100-103), my_compensation (line 125-128), documents_list (line 152-155), policies_list (line 176-179), and receive_test_webhook (line 202-203). While these endpoints also require Bearer token or session authentication, CSRF tokens provide defense-in-depth protection against cross-origin attacks.

In document_list, when filtering by employee (line 93: qs = qs.filter(employee=form.cleaned_data['employee'])), the code re-applies visibility scope at line 96 (qs = qs.filter(pk__in=_visible_documents_for(request.user).values('pk'))). This is correct defense-in-depth, but the implementation uses a subquery which could cause performance issues at scale. More critically, the employee filter allows managers/employees to filter by any employee ID they specify, potentially confirming existence of other employees in the system.
